standard_prerequisites.name: The sentences T(M,w) and E(M,w)
standard_prerequisites.statement: T(M,w) is the author's sentence collecting the axioms that describe the initial configuration and the transition steps of M on w; E(M,w) is the existential sentence expressing that at some time and square the machine is in a state scanning a symbol whose transition is undefined.
standard_prerequisites.use: The proof instantiates the validity of the implication between these two sentences at the structure it builds (source lines 1876-1890).

standard_prerequisites.name: The structure M with domain the natural numbers
standard_prerequisites.statement: The Lang L_M-structure M on the natural numbers interpreting 0 as zero, the prime function as successor, < as less-than, and the predicates Q_q and S_sigma as the relations of being, at time n, in state q scanning square m, respectively containing symbol sigma at square m.
standard_prerequisites.use: The structure is defined at source lines 1867-1887 and is the only structure at which the assumed validity is instantiated.

core_obligations: Construct the structure M with domain Nat interpreting the non-logical symbols of Lang L_M as the arithmetic operations and as the two families of predicates Q_q and S_sigma given by the run of M on w (source lines 1867-1887).
Instantiate the assumed validity of T(M,w) implies E(M,w) at M and verify that M satisfies T(M,w), so that M satisfies E(M,w) as well (source lines 1876-1888).

Unpack the satisfaction of the existential sentence E(M,w) into a pair of numbers and a state/symbol pair with delta(q,sigma) undefined, and read off from the definition of M that M started on w has, after that many steps, entered state q while scanning sigma with an undefined transition, i.e. has halted (source lines 1888-1893).

proof_roadmap.step: Define the Lang L_M-structure M on Nat: arithmetic operations and the predicates Q_q and S_sigma as the run relations.
Apply the assumed validity of T(M,w) implies E(M,w) to M and conclude that M satisfies E(M,w).
Unpack the existential satisfaction into q, sigma with delta(q,sigma) undefined and translate it back into the halting of M on w.

difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the author's own lemma lem:halt-if-valid at source lines 1861-1864: if the sentence T(M,w) implies E(M,w) is valid, then M halts on input w. The proof at source lines 1866-1894 is the semantic converse of a syntactic reduction and is not a routine computation. It has to build the specific Lang L_M-structure M with domain the natural numbers which interprets 0 as zero, the prime function as successor, < as less-than, and the predicates Q_q and S_sigma as the sets of pairs (m,n) recording where the machine is at time n; then instantiate the assumed validity at that structure and at a suitable variable assignment, translate the satisfaction of T(M,w) into the fact that the structure describes the run, unpack the satisfaction of the existential E(M,w) into a pair (q,sigma) with delta undefined, and finally read that back as a genuine halting computation. Each of those translations is a separate step and none of them is stated in the counted lemma. No result outside the retained text is used.
